papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.instructions: Write your name, class and register number on all the work you hand in. Write in dark blue or black pen. You may use a pencil for any diagrams, graphs, tables or rough working. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. There are forty questions in this section. Answer all questions. For each question, there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. A copy of the Periodic Table is printed on page 20. The use of an approved scientific calculator is expected, where appropriate.

questions.stem:
A student wants to carry out an experiment to follow the rate of the reaction between hydrochloric acid and marble chips.

CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + CO₂ + H₂O

Which diagrams show apparatus that is suitable for this experiment?

figures.description: Four numbered apparatus set-ups. 1: a stoppered round-bottomed flask containing hydrochloric acid and marble chips, with a delivery tube from the side of the neck leading under an inverted graduated measuring cylinder standing in a trough of water (gas collected over water). 2: an open beaker containing hydrochloric acid and marble chips standing on an electronic balance. 3: a burette containing hydrochloric acid clamped above an open conical flask containing marble chips; no gas collection. 4: a conical flask containing hydrochloric acid and marble chips, closed with a two-hole stopper; one hole holds a vertical tube fitted with a tap, the other a delivery tube connected to a horizontal gas syringe.

questions.notes: Handwritten cross next to diagram 3 ignored.

questions.stem:
A mixture containing equal volumes of two liquids that mix completely but do not react together is placed in the apparatus shown and heated until the thermometer first shows a steady reading.

At which position will there be the highest proportion of the liquid with the higher boiling point?

options.label: A
options.text: position A – at the mouth of the receiving conical flask (distillate)

options.label: B
options.text: position B – near the top of the fractionating column

options.label: C
options.text: position C – at the bottom of the fractionating column

options.label: D
options.text: position D – inside the round-bottomed flask, just above the boiling liquid

figures.description: Fractional distillation apparatus. A round-bottomed flask containing liquid is heated from below (arrow labelled heat). A fractionating column packed with beads rises vertically from the flask; a thermometer is inserted at the top with its bulb level with the side arm. The side arm leads to a sloping Liebig condenser with 'cold water in' at the lower end and 'water out' at the upper end, delivering into a conical flask. Position labels: A at the mouth of the receiving conical flask; B near the top of the fractionating column; C at the bottom of the fractionating column; D inside the round-bottomed flask just above the liquid surface.

questions.notes: Options are positions marked on the diagram; option text is a description of where each lettered label points, not printed text.

questions.stem:
X and Y are both elements, one of which is a non-metal.

1 mole of X is added to 1 mole of Y and they are heated together.

X and Y react completely to form substance Z.

Substance Z cannot be easily separated to form X and Y.

Three statements are given.

1 Y must be the non-metal.
2 X and Y formed a compound on heating.
3 Substance Z has the empirical formula XY.

Which statements are correct?
Which molecule has only four electrons involved in covalent bonds?
questions.notes: The original option area beside the printed A–D letters is blank; the options appear as an overlaid typed insert 'A. Cl2  B. CO2  C. H2S  D. N2' in a different, larger font. Transcribed from that insert. Faint pencil specks beside A and B ignored.

questions.stem:
Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed with copper electrodes.

What is the equation for the reaction occurring at the anode?

Three statements about fuel cells are given.

1 A hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell requires a continuous input of fuel and oxygen.
2 In a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, hydrogen is burned in oxygen to produce electricity.
3 When a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell is operating, water is the only chemical product.

Which statements are correct?

Which statements about the energy changes during a chemical reaction are correct?

1 The activation energy, Eₐ, is the maximum energy the colliding particles must have in order to react.
2 During an endothermic reaction, thermal energy is taken in from the surroundings leading to a decrease in the temperature of the surroundings.
3 The making of chemical bonds is an exothermic process.
questions.notes: Question number circled by hand; ignored. 'Ea' is printed without a subscript.

questions.stem:
Under certain conditions, nitrogen reacts with oxygen to form N₂O.

2N₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2N₂O(g)

The reaction pathway diagram is shown.

What is the activation energy of the reverse reaction?

figures.description: Reaction pathway (energy profile) diagram: vertical axis 'energy', horizontal axis 'progress of reaction'. Reactants 2N₂(g) + O₂(g) at a lower level; curve rises to a peak then falls to products 2N₂O(g) at a higher level than the reactants. An arrow from the reactant level up to the peak is labelled +447 kJ/mol (forward activation energy). An arrow from the reactant level (dashed line) up to the product level is labelled +164 kJ/mol (enthalpy change).

questions.stem:
Two reactions each produce a gaseous product.

The reactions are performed separately using the same conditions of temperature and pressure.

The volume of gas formed in each experiment is measured over time and the results are plotted in the graph shown.

At which point is the rate of production of gas the greatest?

figures.description: Graph of volume of gas (vertical axis) against time (horizontal axis), both starting at 0. Two lines from the origin: a curve that rises steeply at first then levels off to a horizontal plateau, and a straight line of constant, smaller gradient that eventually crosses above the plateau. Point A is on the steep initial part of the curve near the origin; point B is on the flat plateau of the curve; point C is partway along the straight line; point D is at the upper end of the straight line, above where it crosses the plateau.

questions.notes: Pencil over-tracing on the curve near its bend and an extra handwritten 0 at the origin ignored. Options are points marked on the graph.
